stem: Tank A holds 300 liters of water and is drained at a constant rate of 6 liters per minute. At the same time, Tank B, which holds 40 liters of water, is filled at a constant rate of 7 liters per minute. Which of the following describes all times \(t\), in minutes, during which Tank A holds more water than Tank B and Tank B holds at least 100 liters?
solution: Tank A holds more: \(300 - 6t > 40 + 7t\), so \(260 > 13t\) and \(t < 20\).
Tank B holds at least 100 liters: \(40 + 7t \ge 100\), so \(t \ge \frac{60}{7}\).

explanation.A: Incorrect. At \(t = 20\), both tanks hold 180 liters, so Tank A does not hold more water than Tank B.
explanation.B: Incorrect. This uses only the first condition and ignores the requirement that Tank B hold at least 100 liters.
explanation.C: Incorrect. This adds 40 to 300 instead of subtracting it, which gives \(340 > 13t\).
explanation.D: Correct. Tank A holds more water while \(t < 20\), and Tank B holds at least 100 liters once \(t \ge \frac{60}{7}\).
